conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you.  

Today I’ll be using a short screening tool called the Edinburgh Postpartum/Postnatal Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s just 10 questions about your mood and thoughts over the past week. It helps us spot moms who might need a little extra support, because feeling overwhelmed is incredibly common and nothing to be ashamed of.  

Everything you share stays confidential within our care team; the only exception is if you tell me you might hurt yourself or someone else, and then we’d work together on keeping you safe. There are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you today.  

When you’re ready, we’ll go through the questions one by one. Most moms finish in about five minutes.  

Let’s start: Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[small half-smile, eyes tired]  
“I can still laugh… like when my husband makes a goofy face at the baby. But it feels kind of muted—like I have to remind myself it’s okay to enjoy the moment. Some days I’m just too worn out to find much funny.”
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Mostly yes, but it takes more effort than it used to—sometimes I feel like I’m pretending to laugh so people don’t worry.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to little things—like my morning coffee or when the baby gives me one of those gummy smiles—but the excitement isn’t as strong as before. Sometimes I plan an outing and then feel kind of “meh” when it actually happens.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... a couple of times this week. Like when the baby wouldn't settle at 3 a.m., my brain jumped straight to "I'm probably doing something wrong." I know rationally that newborns just cry, but in the moment I still catch myself thinking it's my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A few times, yeah. The other night the baby sneezed a couple of times and my mind raced to “What if he’s getting really sick?” Even when everything’s quiet, I’ll suddenly feel this knot in my stomach like I’m forgetting something important, even though I can’t name what it is.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panicky… more like this sudden rush of “what-if” that makes my heart race. Yesterday, while folding laundry, I had a quick flash that something awful might happen to the baby, and for a minute I felt shaky and short-of-breath. It passed, but it left me unsettled.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah... some days it feels like the minute I finish one thing—feeding, changing, pumping—there’s already another pile of laundry or a text I forgot to answer. I’m not drowning, but I keep thinking, “How am I going to keep this up?” and then I feel guilty for complaining.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t say I’m “so unhappy,” but I do have trouble turning my brain off. Once the baby’s finally down, I lie there running through the next day’s to-do list or replaying every little hiccup. I probably drift off an hour or two later than I want, a few nights a week.
I have felt sad or miserable

I get little waves of sadness—like when I’m rocking the baby and suddenly feel like I’m missing something, or when I see photos of myself before he was born and think, “I should feel happier than this.” It’s not all day, but most days there’s at least a moment where I feel kind of blue.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Not really. I teared up once this week when the baby wouldn’t latch and I was running on three hours of sleep, but I didn’t full-on cry. Most days I just feel kind of flat rather than tearful.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt tired or overwhelmed, but I haven’t had any thoughts like that.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Patient: Anonymous postpartum client (self-report)

Symptoms / Concerns endorsed  
- Anhedonia: reduced enjoyment of previously pleasurable activities  
- Low mood: “waves of sadness,” feeling “flat,” “blue” most days  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame when baby fusses  
- Unwarranted worry, “what-if” rumination, nocturnal mental “replay”  
- Episodic physiologic anxiety (heart racing, shakiness, shortness of breath) without clear trigger  
- Sense of being overwhelmed by daily tasks, guilt for “complaining”  
- Initial insomnia 2–3 nights/week related to intrusive thoughts and planning  
- Denies tearful crying spells and denies any self-harm ideation

Patterns / Risk indicators  
- Sub-syndromal depressive features with prominent anxiety  
- Functional impact: sleep disruption, reduced enthusiasm, self-doubt about parenting competence  
- No safety concerns (no suicidal or infanticidal ideation reported)

Screening significance  
Findings suggest possible mild–moderate postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; does not meet threshold for immediate safety intervention but warrants formal clinical assessment (PHQ-9, GAD-7, EPDS), psychoeducation, and consideration of supportive or evidence-based treatment options.
